strategy.summary: Platinenwerk Lausitz is a sound, private, mid-sized PCBA maker. It has been our single source for the HB smart pump control board since 2014 and owns the tooling. We are a small customer to it. It has sold below our should-cost for four renewals to keep the volume. It now asks a formally valid +8 %, which the electronic-components and labour indices largely support; the copper argument is weak. Leverage is theirs. There is little price room, and squeezing it risks the supply of an A-part. Our real levers are terms: binding volume, 24 months, punctual or faster payment and possibly an index clause on PPI-C2611. Its worsening quality (and slipping delivery) is legitimate leverage to secure a ppm commitment rather than to force price. Moves above the threshold go to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks, so rounds are slow and packages must be complete.
strategy.decision_maker: Key account manager handles correspondence; price changes above the threshold need its pricing committee, which meets every two weeks (doc:20260417-70550-M1).

price_view.reasoning: The indices justify nearly the full ask, and the current price is below should-cost. Its history of settling well below its ask suggests some give, but its margin is exhausted. A realistic landing is mid-way, bought with volume, length and quality terms rather than cost attacks. The should-cost estimate is uncertain, but the gap exceeds its error band.

findings.text: Price sits below our should-cost: current EUR 34.35 vs should-cost EUR 37.24 (no margin included), i.e. -7.8%. Even the asked EUR 37.10 is still ~0.4% below full cost before any margin. The should-cost confidence is only 5% (error about 5%), but the gap exceeds that band. No room to push price down on cost grounds.

Cost drivers back an increase of about 8%: PPI-C2611 electronic components +13.5% in 12 months at weight 0.55 (~+7.4% on price), now at its 36-month peak and near its all-time high; LCI-C labour +2.7% at weight 0.2 (~+0.5%). The combined ~+7.95% matches the 8.0% ask almost exactly. The remaining 25% of cost (overhead and other) has no index. Industrial power -43% vs 2022 may soften overhead, but that is general market news, not about this supplier.

The letter's copper argument is weak for a 0.2 kg PCBA. The copper notation of +48% is for cables and is not one of the part's drivers. The 'boards +41%' news figure contradicts the official PPI of +13.5%. Rebut with the index records rather than the news headlines.

Price history: price was cut from 35.54 (2023) to 34.21 (2025), then rose 0.4% to 34.35 for 2026. The supplier has repeatedly accepted below-full-cost prices to keep the volume. The ask is far above its historic pattern: it asked +0.9% on average and settled -1.1% on average. The last round asked +2.1% and settled +0.4%. Increases above 2% need approval from its pricing committee.

Room on price is limited: a realistic landing is roughly +4% to +6% (EUR 35.7 to 36.4), with a floor near the labour-only and part-index pass-through. Trading terms beats contesting the cost logic. Possible trades are a PPI-C2611 index clause, the volume rise from 18,540 to 19,920 units, longer commitment and faster payment. Weak quality (701 ppm vs peer median 457) and delivery (85.7% vs 95% target) give non-cost leverage. The contract notice was valid.

findings.text: Decision ladder: the key account manager cannot grant or accept price changes above 2 % alone; a pricing committee decides and meets only every two weeks. Each counter-proposal beyond ±2 % costs a two-week cycle, so rounds are slow. We should put complete, well-argued term sheets in early (notice ends of year 2026, price effective 2027-01-01).

The 8 % ask on part:350030 (34.35 to 37.10 from 2027-01-01) is formally correct, with 104 days' notice against the 90 required. It argues copper and electronic components and appeals to years of reliable supply. The letter is generic ('Dear Sir or Madam'), with no cost breakdown. Its claim is partly backed: the electronic components index rose +13.5 % at a 55 % cost share, about +7.4 %, and labour adds about +0.5 %.

The supplier is under real margin pressure on this part. Should-cost is EUR 37.24 and its current price is 7.8 % below it. Notes on 4 events record that it accepted below full cost to keep the volume, and its price has fallen 3.3 % since 2023. If the part is stabilise or secure_supply, pushing it further below cost carries a health charge and makes it more willing to walk. It values volume: forecast 19,920 against 18,540 ordered in the last 12 months.

The company is financially sound and stable: 88 M EUR turnover, 39.5 % equity ratio, credit index 150 unchanged, VDA 6.3 grade A, ISO 9001 renewed. Our spend is about 0.7 % of its turnover, so we are a small customer. There are no signs of financial stress, and it could afford to drop us.

Our payment behaviour is a sensitivity. We pay 88.4 % of invoices late, 5.2 days on average and at most 11 days, and 6 invoices are unpaid. Contract terms are 45 days net, already shorter than our 60-day standard. Faster or more punctual payment is a cheap trade it will value; we should expect it to raise lateness.

Weaknesses on its side: quality worsened to 701 ppm from 461, against a peer median of 457, with 8 complaints and 2 8Ds not closed. On-time delivery fell to 85.7 %, below the 95 % contract target. Historically it settles well below its ask: last time it asked +2.1 % and settled +0.4 %. The news about apprentice training is noise.

findings.text: Contract ctr:4600070550 is a framework agreement running 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30. Prices are fixed per calendar year, and a change needs at least 90 days' written notice before year-end. The supplier's letter of 2026-09-19 gave 104 days' notice, so the request for +8% to EUR 37.10 from 2027-01-01 is formally valid. We cannot reject it on procedure; we have to negotiate on substance.

The contract renews automatically for 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice, which means notice by 2027-04-01. Termination is technically open to us, but an exit is not credible in the short term because of single sourcing. Payment is 45 days net against our 60-day standard, which favours the supplier and is a tradeable term. Delivery is DAP with 56 days' lead time.

The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per complaint. Actual on-time delivery is 85.7% (88.0% a year earlier). Rolling ppm is 701 against a peer median of 457, with 8 complaints and 2 8Ds still open. The supplier is breaching its contractual targets, which gives us legitimate leverage.

Over four events (EV-2023 to EV-2026) the supplier settled below its ask each time, on average 2.1 pp below. The last renewal asked +2.1% and settled at +0.4%. Every event is noted 'accepted below full cost to keep the volume'. Its price has fallen 3.3% since 2023, and should-cost (EUR 37.24) is about 7.8% above the current price. Its margin is therefore probably exhausted, and its +8% ask is far larger than in past rounds.

Dependency is asymmetric against us. The supplier holds a 100% quota as our only approved source since 2014 and owns the tooling, and we have no RFQ history. Our spend of about EUR 636k is only about 0.7% of its EUR 88M turnover. Its finances are sound (equity ratio 39.5%, credit index 150, unchanged), so it can afford to walk away.

An end to selling below full cost
Faster payment, or at least punctual payment (we pay on average 5.2 days late)
Volume commitment and a longer contract term
Possibly an index clause on electronic components

findings.text: Quality is deteriorating sharply: rolling 12-month ppm jumped to 701 (13 complaints, 8 QNs) from 451 a quarter earlier and 461 a year earlier, against a peer median of 457. Since June 2026 there have been five supplier-caused QNs on part:350030 (coating, dimension, leakage x2, wrong certificate). The two latest are still without a closed 8D, although the scorecard shows 0 overdue. This is our strongest performance lever against the 8% increase.

The defect pattern is recurrent rather than random. Leakage at test, porosity, dimension out of tolerance and burr keep coming back from 2024 to 2026, which suggests corrective actions are not sticking. 17 of 21 QNs on part:350030 were supplier-caused, but only EUR 1,950 has been recharged at the EUR 150 flat fee. That fee is far below the real cost to us of a defective control board. Note that per-lot ppm values (up to 7692) are jumpy; cite the rolling scorecard figure instead.

Delivery has improved over two years but is slipping again. On-time delivery rose from 68.2% (2024Q3) to a peak of 91.7% (2026Q2), then fell to 85.7% (2026Q3). That is still well short of the 95% contract target, though slightly above the peer median of 84.6%. Average lateness is 9.5 days, with a maximum of 15. Requested and confirmed dates are now aligned (85.7% against both), so it is not hiding behind its confirmations. The supplier is still class A green, which softens the argument somewhat.

Volume outlook is stable to slightly up. The 2026-09 forecast is 19,920 pieces for the next 12 months against 18,540 ordered in the last 12 months (+7.4%), and the forecast has been shared with the supplier. Over 2023 to 2026, volume has run steadily at about 18-22k pieces per year. Offering a commitment on this volume is a trade worth something to the supplier. Monthly dips (Dec 1,000, Aug 620) are seasonal.

Order history anchors the current price at EUR 34.35. Since EUR 35.54 in 2023 the price has fallen 3.3%, which the supplier will use to argue it has already given back. Its own should-cost and index arguments support part of the increase.

arguments.text: We have sold this board below our full cost for four consecutive renewals to keep your volume: -1.8 % in 2024, -2.0 % in 2025 and only +0.4 % in 2026. Even EUR 37.10 barely reaches our cost, with no margin on it. This is cost recovery, not a margin grab.

Electronic components, the bulk of a PCBA's cost, are at their 36-month peak: PPI electronic components +13.5 % in 12 months. Producer prices for assembled boards are +41 % year on year, so the market has moved far more than our 8 %.
Labour costs in manufacturing rose +2.7 %, and labour is a real share of our conversion cost.
Our notice was formally correct under clause 3.1: 104 days given against 90 required. The price is fixed per calendar year, so 2027 is the year to correct it.
Our delivery has improved markedly, from 68 % OTD in 2024Q3 to around 86-92 %. We remain a solid, certified partner with an A rating.

weak_points: Our quality has worsened: ppm reached 701 in the last 12 months, 13 complaints, two 8Ds still open, and recurring leakage, porosity and dimension defects. The customer can rightly push a ppm commitment.
OTD of 85.7 % is still below the contractual 95 % target, and OTD slipped in the latest quarter.
Copper is a minor cost driver for a 0.2 kg PCBA. That part of our letter is weak and should not be leaned on.
Industrial power prices are -43 % against 2022, which offsets part of our cost.

Their own index basket (0.55 x 13.5 % + 0.2 x 2.7 %) gives roughly +8 % on the whole, so we are at the ceiling, not above it. Our history of settling well below our ask invites them to expect a discount.
Changes above 2 % need our pricing committee, so we are slow and cannot improvise in the room.
They are a small customer for us, so we cannot easily threaten to walk; we also want the volume.
The should-cost estimate behind our cost argument is low-confidence.
wants: Binding annual volume of about 20,000 pcs, in line with their forecast of 19,920.
Extension to 24 months beyond 2027-06, or a firm renewal.
Punctual payment: they pay 88 % of invoices late, so honouring 45 days, or better 30 days.
An index clause on PPI-C2611 for the component share, in exchange for a lower base increase.
A reasonable ppm target with a realistic ramp and the chargeback kept at EUR 150 rather than raised.
red_lines: No price below about EUR 36.40 (+6 %) without binding volume, a 24-month term and an index clause; we will not sell below cost a fifth year.
No higher chargeback or ppm penalty without a price recognising the cost.
No effective date later than 2027-01-01 without compensation.
red_team.opening: Thank them for the long partnership and acknowledge the quality issues openly, offering an 8D action plan. Restate +8 % to EUR 37.10, grounded in the four below-cost renewals and the electronic-components index, while dropping the copper emphasis. Signal that a complete package (binding 20k volume, 24 months, punctual payment, PPI-C2611 index clause) lets us take a lower base, around +6 to +6.5 %, to our pricing committee. Ask them to send all their terms in one go, since the committee meets every two weeks.

rebuttals.answer: We recognise that you have supported us over several renewals and we value that; a sustainable price matters to us on a strategic board. At the same time, our renewals have consistently closed well below the opening request, and what we pay today is the honest starting point. We would rather recover your cost through binding volume, a longer term and punctual payment than through the full increase on the unit price alone.

The rise in electronic component prices is real and we take it into account. The general assembled-board figure is a market headline, not a measure of this board's cost, and the component index has now peaked, so it may fall during the contract. If a fixed price feels too risky for you, we are open to discussing a clause on the component index at its share. That would protect both of us without fixing a peak level for a whole year.
Agreed, labour costs have risen. However, labour is only a modest share of the board, so it explains a small part of the request, not the bulk of it.

We do not dispute the notice; it was correct, and we are treating your letter as the start of a fair renewal. The clause allows a change to be requested. It does not set the amount, which remains a matter for negotiation between us.

Your delivery has improved over the past two years, and we appreciate it. It is still below the target in our quality agreement and slipped in the latest period. We would like a joint improvement plan and a ppm commitment to be part of this agreement.

Copper is a minor input for a light assembled board like this one, so the cable copper notation says little about its cost. At the same time, industrial power prices have fallen markedly over recent years, which eases part of your conversion cost.

press: We would welcome your corrective action plan for the recurring leakage, porosity and dimensional defects, and we would like to agree a ppm target as part of this renewal.
Would a binding annual volume in line with our shared forecast, together with a longer term, allow you to revise your proposal?
Since copper plays only a small role in an assembled board of this weight, could we focus our discussion on the electronic component and labour drivers?
The lower industrial power prices should also ease part of your conversion cost, and we would appreciate seeing this reflected in your proposal.
To fit your pricing committee's cycle, we would like to send you a complete package, so could you let us know when it next meets?
We are also putting our invoice payments back on time and would be glad to confirm punctual payment as part of the agreement.
